newsitem.title: USA: Biomatrix gets FDA nod on knee treatment.
newsitem.headline: Biomatrix gets FDA nod on knee treatment.

text.p: Biomatrix Inc said Wednesday that it received U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval to market Synvisc in the United States.
Synvisc is Biomatrix' product for the intra-articular treatment of osteoarthritis of the knee.
Wyeth-Ayerst Laboratories, a division of American Home Products Corp, has a marketing and distribution agreement with Biomatrix to sell Synvisc in the United States.
Synvisc is used to relieve knee pain due to osteoarthritis, a joint disease that affects nearly 16 million Americans.
It is used for patients who do not get adequate relief from simple painkillers or from exercise and physical therapy.
This approval represents the culmination of 10 years of global clinical research and post- marketing studies in Europe, Canada and the United States, Biomatrix said.
Biomatrix said it will manufacture the product for sale by Wyeth-Ayerst and expects Synvisc to be available in the United States this fall.
As part of this agreement, Biomatrix said it will receive a $12 million milestone payment from Wyeth-Ayerst related to the FDA's approval to market Synvisc in the U.S.
